native.documentPipelineIntro: A practical PDF-to-knowledge flow: normalize PDFs locally, archive and OCR them in Paperless, enrich them with Paperless-AI, then work with the corpus in AnythingLLM with Paperless-ngx integrated for quick checks.

securePlatform.title: Secure AI platform engineering
securePlatform.lead: The goal is not to accumulate AI tools. It is to operate models, agents, MCP tools and knowledge pipelines behind explicit security, reliability, cost and governance boundaries.

gateway.title: Controlled model gateway
gateway.description: Route local and remote inference through LiteLLM so clients share authentication, budgets, fallbacks, telemetry and provider policy instead of calling models directly.

identity.title: Identity, secrets & data boundaries
identity.description: Keep credentials server-side, constrain access by workload, and separate sensitive prompts, documents and tenant data from public or lower-trust execution paths.

mcp.title: MCP & agent trust boundaries
mcp.description: Treat tools as privileged capabilities: scope what agents can call, isolate execution, minimize filesystem and network reach, and keep human approval for destructive actions.

rag.title: RAG provenance & lifecycle
rag.description: Track source provenance, ingestion state and retention across Paperless, OCR and retrieval pipelines so generated answers remain traceable to controlled knowledge.

observability.title: Observability, evaluation & FinOps
observability.description: Trace prompts, latency, model selection and token cost with Langfuse and operational metrics, then evaluate quality separately instead of relying on anecdotal output checks.

governance.title: Governance by design
governance.description: Map technical controls to GDPR, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 concerns: accountability, access control, evidence, data residency, supplier risk and model-use policy.

outcomes.privacy: local-first privacy with controlled remote fallback
outcomes.policy: one policy layer for models and agents
outcomes.providers: replaceable providers instead of vendor lock-in

architecture.title: My AI platform architecture
architecture.intro: A local-first platform structured as layers rather than a product catalogue. LiteLLM is the central control plane connecting interfaces, models, tools, workflows, and observability.
architecture.privacyCopy: Routine workloads prefer Ollama inside the homelab. Routing through LiteLLM keeps one shared routing and protection policy before any remote inference.
architecture.costCopy: Redis caching, fallbacks, and centralized routing reduce unnecessary remote calls and avoid coupling clients to a single model.
architecture.measurableCopy: Langfuse, Opik, and Prometheus separate LLM observability, quality evaluation, and operational metrics while preserving a coherent platform view.

guide.title: My AI platform journey
guide.lead: The page now follows the platform layers from agents through governance. Use this journey to jump directly to an architectural responsibility.

globalTools.title: Global AI components
globalTools.lead: Shared capabilities decoupled from agents: execution, knowledge, and isolation can be consumed by Open WebUI, agents, and workflows.
globalTools.terminal: Self-hosted terminal exposing a simple API so agents and automation can execute commands and manipulate files in a controlled environment.
globalTools.openrag: Shared RAG layer fed by the vetted PDF corpus produced through Paperless. OpenRAG combines Langflow workflows, Docling parsing, and OpenSearch-backed retrieval to provide document ingestion, search, and chat in one stack. Its APIs can then be wrapped by a custom MCP server so AI interfaces and agents reuse a common retrieval surface instead of reimplementing knowledge-base access.
globalTools.openshell: Sandboxed runtime for autonomous agents with isolation, declarative policies, and controlled network, filesystem, process, and credential access.

observability.title: LLM observability, evaluation & FinOps
observability.lead: A unified view of quality, traces, costs, tokens, and latency: evaluate LLM applications, monitor production behavior, and apply FinOps discipline to model consumption.
observability.opik: Open-source platform for evaluating, testing, and monitoring LLM applications, useful for comparing model outputs and tracking production quality.
observability.langfuse: Open-source LLM observability platform for traces, prompts, scores, costs, and latency. Langfuse collects telemetry from LiteLLM and the MCP server to provide a cross-platform view of AI calls.

usage.description: Track ChatGPT and Codex usage across credits, tokens, models, activity, and consumption. Available analytics depend on the workspace plan; Codex also exposes usage and limit details in supported account settings.

workflow.title: Workflow & orchestration
workflow.lead: Three complementary roles: n8n for rapidly composing automations, Temporal for durable execution, and Langflow for experimenting with and assembling AI flows.
workflow.n8n: Visual automation layer for rapidly connecting APIs, data, agents, and homelab services.
workflow.temporal: Durable orchestration for stateful, long-running, critical workflows: retries, persistent state, timers, human-in-the-loop steps, and LLM activities.
workflow.langflow: Visual workbench for prototyping LLM chains, agents, tools, and RAG before productionizing them in orchestration and service layers.
workflow.opencommit: OpenCommit complements the development workflow with consistent Conventional Commit messages; it intentionally remains outside the orchestration layer.
